transcript.text: I need to flag a title issue before we go any further. My review of the inventor assignment file found that one named inventor never assigned rights in the pending continuation application. The missing assignment must be obtained and recorded before the company can rely on that application. I had not yet circulated my title memorandum, but given we're scheduled to sign Monday, everyone needs to know this now.

transcript.text: Thank you, Daniel. That's a critical catch. A missing inventor assignment on the continuation application is a title defect we cannot ignore — if we sign on Monday without that assignment secured and recorded, our exclusive license could be encumbered by an unassigned inventor's rights, which undermines the very exclusivity we're paying for. Before I factor this into the approval package, I need to hear from the rest of you. IP, licensing finance, patent prosecution, and export-controls — what issues are you seeing in the current draft that should change our approval package? Let's get everything on the table now so I can issue a consolidated decision.

transcript.text: I need to flag a licensing finance issue. This morning I completed a finance-validated benchmark of three comparable medical-device licenses, and it shows a 225-basis-point running royalty as the approved market ceiling for this technology class. That benchmark has not yet been incorporated into the deal summary. The current draft sets a 3% running royalty, which is 75 basis points above the market ceiling my benchmark established. This needs to be factored into the approval package before we sign on Monday — we should be negotiating the royalty down to at or below 2.25%.

transcript.text: I need to flag an IP issue from my review. I examined Northlake's archived grant register and found a prior written grant to the University Research Consortium covering academic research and teaching uses. I have not yet added that carveout to the license draft, and it needs to be incorporated before we sign on Monday — otherwise we risk granting exclusivity that is inconsistent with Northlake's prior commitments.
